editorial.headline: Umrah and Special-Hajj Travel: Open Nationally, Available in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers the assembly and sale of Umrah and special-Hajj travel packages, with a fully open national foreign-ownership position and no Bali moratorium block.
editorial.body:
An Umrah and special-Hajj pilgrimage travel bureau plans and assembles travel packages for these forms of worship. Those packages may be channelled through travel agents or sold directly to consumers, online or in person. The activity reaches beyond the itinerary itself: it includes services connected to the package sold, including transport, accommodation and meals, as well as handling travel documents such as passports, visas and equivalent documents. In practical terms, this is the organising business behind a pilgrimage journey, from the package design through the travel services and documentation that support it.

The activity is open at every stated business scale: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. That breadth matters because the record does not confine the activity to a single size of operator. A bureau may operate around the planning and sale of pilgrimage packages while using either agent distribution or direct consumer sales, and may do so through digital or offline channels. Its defined scope keeps the focus on Umrah and special-Hajj travel packages and the services attached to those packages.

Nationally, the activity is marked TERBUKA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. Put plainly, the national position permits full foreign ownership. Bali does not reverse that position for this activity. The province’s permanent, island-wide PMA moratorium applies to all Low and Medium-Low risk activities. Here, however, the OSS risk at the Besar scale is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so the activity is not blocked by that moratorium. The Bali status is therefore OK_or_HIGHER_RISK: a foreign investor can register this activity in Bali under the position recorded here, rather than finding its national openness cancelled at the provincial level.

That distinction is the useful one for a founder reading the code closely. The national foreign-ownership position is fully open, while Bali’s result rests on the activity’s stated risk position at the Besar scale and its consequent exclusion from the Low and Medium-Low risk moratorium. The record supports a clear conclusion: this is a pilgrimage-travel bureau activity with room for operators from Mikro through Besar, and an open PMA path that remains available in Bali.
